newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan proposes Habib Bank division before sale.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan proposes Habib Bank division before sale.

text.p: Pakistan is to invite new bids from prospective buyers of state-owned Habib Bank Ltd, due for privatisation this year, according to a Privatisation Commission document obtained by Reuters on Sunday.

It said the caretaker government wanted to restructure the bank and seek fresh bids from short-listed investors, who include: Lehman Brothers International (Europe) with First Capital Securities Corp Ltd; ABN-Amro Bank with Ernst Young and Anjum Asim Shahid and Co; Citibank; and CS First Boston with BMA Capital Management.
The restructuring proposals call for Habib Bank to be split into two or more banks, a quarter of its employees to be offered severance payments and a fifth of its branches to be closed.
Pakistan had originally set June 1996 as the target date for the sale of a 26 percent stake in Habib Bank to a strategic investor who would take management control.
But the sale was delayed after an attempt to privatise state-owned United Bank Ltd failed last year. Pakistan has already privatised Muslim Commercial Bank and Allied Bank.
